title: Zelenskyy Warns U.S. Siding With Russia Would Be a 'Historic Mistake'
snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged President Trump to reconsider recent sanctions waivers and fuel agreements with Moscow, warning that aligning with Russia would undermine both nations.
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued a stark warning to Washington on Sunday, declaring that any U.S. move to formally align with Russian President Vladimir Putin would constitute a "historic mistake," even as he expressed hope for continued partnership with President Donald Trump.

In an interview on NBC's "Meet the Press," Zelenskyy reflected on a turbulent stretch in U.S.-Ukraine relations marked by White House decisions to waive bipartisan Russian sanctions and strike a global diesel agreement with Moscow aimed at lowering gas prices.

Strained Alliances and Policy Shifts

"We want to trust him," Zelenskyy said regarding Trump. "I hope that he will change his decisions, because I think that it’s all mistakes, and it will not help us, and it will not help United States."

Trump recently signed an executive order waiving fresh sanctions passed by Congress to target Russian oil and gas revenues. The administration framed the move as vital to U.S. national interests, coinciding with an arrangement with Putin to release hundreds of thousands of tons of Russian diesel to ease soaring energy costs. Zelenskyy countered that the rising fuel prices stem from disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz rather than Ukraine, warning that economic concessions will only "strengthen Putin in his will to occupy us."

Intelligence Pauses and Technological Hurdles

The Ukrainian president also highlighted recent operational setbacks, noting that U.S. intelligence sharing was temporarily halted, briefly blinding Ukrainian forces to incoming ballistic missile threats. Though Zelenskyy confirmed that intelligence channels have since been restored, restrictions remain on Starshield—the military variant of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite network vital for countering jet-powered drones.

Zelenskyy suggested the restrictions on Starlink were implemented following a "message from American government," adding that the service could be fully restored instantly if Trump requested it.

Capitol Hill Pushback and Negotiation Stalls

Defending the administration's actions, Sen. James Lankford (R-Okla.) argued on "Meet the Press" that Trump is seeking a balance between applying pressure on Russia and prioritizing domestic economic concerns. "He’s trying to walk this fine balance... he is choosing the American people first," Lankford said, maintaining that Trump remains committed to forcing both nations to the negotiating table.

Despite Trump's campaign promises to resolve the war swiftly, peace talks remain deadlocked. Russia occupies approximately one-fifth of Ukrainian territory, and Kyiv has rejected Moscow's terms as equivalent to total surrender. Facing an impending winter and severe ammunition shortages, Zelenskyy said he remains open to high-level discussions with U.S. officials to repair the working relationship.
